text: The system shall accept a write of an item only through the one path that every writer inside the platform uses.
rationale: DEC-009. Sources write through Ingestion, agents write what they infer (DEC-010), and a caller that keeps the result of a live read writes it here (DEC-008). A second path into life state is a second path to build and a second path to check, and every refusal in this system would have to be written on it again.

text: The system shall refuse a write of an item that does not state its origin.
rationale: DEC-014 states the contract on both sides. The refusal is the side that cannot be gone around, and it binds a writer for which nobody wrote a requirement. REQ-PL-001 makes each item show its origin, and an item with no origin cannot be given one later.

text: The system shall refuse a write of an item that does not state the time at which the platform received the item.
rationale: DEC-016. The time of receipt is always known to the writer and is never known later. The time of the observation is not refused, because a source does not always supply one.

text: The system shall hold, with each item, the origin that its writer supplied.
rationale: REQ-PL-001. The origin is an external source or an agent, and it is part of what identifies an assertion (DEC-022).

text: The system shall hold, with each item, the time at which the platform received it.
rationale: DEC-016. The time of receipt is always present, and REQ-ST-003 refuses an item that does not carry it. REQ-IN-022 states the supplying side of this pair.

text: The system shall hold the values that an item held before its current value.
rationale: Supersession needs the value that was replaced, and REQ-PL-015 needs the data that a derivation used. A value that the platform does not keep cannot support either.

text: The system shall give, as the current value of an observed item, the value from the most recent observation of that item.
rationale: REQ-PL-001 makes the platform decide which value is current, and not the reader. RSK-PL-006 is the failure that this answers. DEC-011 limits the guarantee to observed values, because a derived value has no identity that a later value replaces.

text: The system shall match an item that arrives against an item that it holds, by the identifier that its writer supplied.
rationale: The platform cannot tell a new item from a later value of an item that it holds without an identifier. REQ-IN-007 and REQ-IN-020 make Ingestion supply one that is stable and unique.

text: The system shall hold that an item no longer exists at its source, when a writer states it.
rationale: DEC-017. A removal at the source is an observation about the item. Supersession does not cover it, because a removal has no later value.

text: The system shall not include an item that no longer exists at its source in the answer to a query for current items.
rationale: DEC-017 keeps the item and the observation against it, and REQ-ST-007 makes that observation the most recent one. This requirement states what a reader sees, so that a reader does not have to filter a cancelled meeting out of an answer.

text: The system shall tell an observed value from a derived value.
rationale: REQ-PL-015. An inference that a reader cannot identify is given as a fact.

text: The system shall hold, with each derived value, the data that the derivation used and the time of the derivation.
rationale: DEC-011. A derived value decays when its inputs move on and nothing replaces it. The reader judges it, and the reader needs the inputs and the time to do so.

text: The system shall hold two assertions about one subject that have different origins.
rationale: DEC-022. Two assertions with two origins are two assertions. To judge which is correct is a judgement about content, and REQ-PL-019 says that the platform does not make one.

text: The system shall give, with each value that it serves, the origin of that value and its times.
rationale: A reader that cannot see where a value came from and when cannot judge it. This is what makes DEC-011 work for a derived value and DEC-022 work for two assertions.

text: The system shall answer a query for the value of an item.
rationale: REQ-PL-002. An agent needs an exact value.

text: The system shall answer a query by meaning, and shall give the items that relate to the subject of the query.
rationale: REQ-PL-002. An agent needs related values as well as exact ones, from one body of data. The criteria for what relates to a subject are TST- entries below this level.

text: The system shall not serve to a caller a part of life state that the position of that caller does not admit.
rationale: REQ-PL-024. Agent Definition declares the position and what it admits, and this boundary refuses (DEC-019).

text: The system shall not accept a write to a part of life state that the position of the writer does not admit.
rationale: REQ-PL-024 states the limit for serving and for writing, and DEC-010 limits what an agent writes in the same way as what it reads. Agent Definition declares the position and this boundary refuses (DEC-019).

text: The system shall make a copy of life state in a location away from the host, one time each day or more often.
rationale: REQ-PL-022 and DEC-004. External Access carries the copy to the external service and does not decide what is copied or when (DEC-020).

text: The system shall restore life state from the copy away from the host.
rationale: A copy that nobody restored is not a copy. REQ-PL-022 is met by the restoration and not by the copy.

text: The copy away from the host shall be in a form that an agent can read when the platform does not run.
rationale: REQ-PL-021 and DEC-004 give the copy two duties. DEC-020 limits the obligation of the platform to the form of the copy, because nothing inside the platform can serve agents while the platform does not run. OPN-007 holds the question of what that form is.

text: The system shall remove the items that a selection states, when the user asks.
rationale: REQ-PL-026. A person removes by kind and by period and not one item at a time: the heart rate of the last week, the browsing history of the last two days. The selection for a removal is the selection that a query already uses, so removal does not need a second way to state which items it means. Everything from one source is one such selection.

text: The system shall remove, with each item that it removes, the values that the item held before.
rationale: REQ-ST-006 keeps the values that an item held before, for supersession and for provenance. A removal that leaves them leaves the data that the user asked to remove, and the user cannot see that it stayed.

text: The system shall not report a write as accepted until it holds the item.
rationale: A writer that gets an acceptance does not send the item again. Ingestion then reports a source that is healthy, because the delivery succeeded from outside, and the item is in no part of the platform.

text: The system shall report, at an interval of TBD, whether life state can be restored from the copy away from the host.
rationale: A copy that nobody restored is not a copy, and RSK-ST-004 is found only by restoring. REQ-ST-020 is the capability to restore; this requirement is how often the platform proves that it still works. The interval depends on what a restoration costs on this host, which is not yet known.

text: The system shall report a write that it refuses.
rationale: REQ-ST-002 and REQ-ST-003 state the refusal. A refusal that nobody hears is data that one system acquired, another refused, and no report names. One requirement covers every reason to refuse, including REQ-ST-018, so a new reason does not need a new report.

text: The system shall give, with a derived value whose inputs it removed, a statement that those inputs are no longer held.
rationale: Removal wins over a derivation. DEC-011 rejected tracking a dependency continuously, and this is not that: REQ-ST-012 already holds the inputs of each derived value, and the system reads them at a removal, which is one action that the user starts.

text: The system shall answer a query for the value of an item within TBD.
rationale: Life state grows and nothing expires (DEC-021), so the time to answer grows with it. The value depends on the host and on what a caller needs. The time for a query by meaning waits for OPN-003 and OPN-023.

text: The system shall accept the declaration of a kind of item. The declaration shall state the form of the items of that kind.
rationale: DEC-025. Without a declared form, nothing can refuse a write that does not match it, and nobody can state what life state contains.

text: The system shall refuse a write of an item whose kind is not declared.
rationale: DEC-025. This is the form that REQ-IN-005 converts a delivery into, and it is the acceptance rule that DEC-014 puts on this side of that contract.

text: The system shall hold, with each declared kind, the origin that declared it.
rationale: DEC-026 lets an agent ask a second agent to declare a kind in its own name. The declaration is only examinable afterwards if it carries the agent that made it, in the same way that DEC-022 makes the origin part of what identifies an assertion.

text: The system shall refuse the declaration of a kind from a writer whose position does not admit it.
rationale: REQ-PL-005 limits an agent to the authority that its position gives. DEC-019 makes each boundary refuse, and a declaration arrives at this one. The refusal is what makes DEC-026 necessary and makes RSK-PL-007 unreachable by this path.

text: The system shall hold, with each item, the time of the observation when the writer supplied that time.
rationale: DEC-016. A source does not always supply a time of observation, so this time is not refused and is never given a default value. REQ-IN-018 states the supplying side of this pair.

text: The system shall answer a query over every item that it holds and that the position of the caller admits.
rationale: REQ-PL-001 holds life state as one body. One body is a property that a caller can observe and not a statement about how the data is held: a caller does not have to know where an item is, and does not have to ask two times. The only partition that a caller sees is position (REQ-PL-024). How the system holds the body is a decision below this level, and MET-005 does not permit a requirement to name a store.

text: The copy away from the host shall be of a state of life state that the system held at one time.
rationale: RSK-ST-004 names a copy that is not consistent as a cause, and no requirement answered it. A copy that is made while writes are in progress holds some items that are new and some that are old, and life state was never in that state. A derived value in such a copy can name inputs that the copy does not hold. REQ-ST-025 finds this after the fact. This requirement states the property and names no mechanism.
